node.2a6321b4ce90763bf0be564e puts offering in Scope; node.6d6e7adc6faa9d94b74c08e5, node.968dbccb08282a4e8a580ae5, node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f and node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 put promotional conditions in Scope. Failed conditions therefore produce OUT_OF_SCOPE rather than the typed negative or compliant result. These may be intended domain restrictions, but the typed questions do not expressly establish that narrower domain.

The offer-level candidates separate the offer's promotional connection from the existence of a non-discount gift component. Unless supplied classifications connect that same gift to the promotion, mixed offers could be overclassified.
SFC-authorised-fund scope follows the circular's introduction, but does not establish the full scope of paragraph 3.11 for other investment products.
Gift status, discount status and offer attribution remain supplied judgments. Neither guaranteed-return status nor underlying-fund-return provenance alone establishes a gift prohibition or exemption.
A compliant or non-prohibited result under the selected gift control does not establish compliance with separate disclosure, advertising or structured-product requirements.
The supplied source establishes no operative date interval. Temporal availability and dependency-wide conflict blocking are runtime policies, not requirements stated in the circular.
